title: Introduce invocation stabilizer and fidelity-aware metric gating
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: we see frequent short-lived bursts (1-10s) that spike per-invocation percentiles and cause noisy alerts even though downstream client perceived latency remains acceptable. This makes SRE triage expensive and obscures real regressions. Summary: add an Invocation Stabilizer service (runtime-side aggregator) plus a fidelity-aware metric gating layer that prevents percentile/alert updates until a configurable minimum of high-fidelity samples are available. The stabilizer computes lightweight per-invocation EWMAs and emits stabilized metrics (invocation.stabilized.{p50,p95,p99}, invocation.stabilized.count) and fidelity tags (fidelity=low|medium|high). The gating layer in PromQL/Alertmanager uses those fidelity tags to mute or route noisy alerts to a lower priority channel until fidelity stabilizes. This PR includes: - the stabilizer implementation in the serving runtime (stateless worker that consumes invocation probes, computes EWMA aggregates, and annotates traces/metrics) - Prometheus rule changes and new recording rules for stabilized series - Alertmanager rule templates and an adjusted SLO alert that is fidelity-gated - Grafana dashboard (dashboard/json) for the stabilizer: time series, fidelity distribution, noise window histogram, and alert-suppression heatmap - playbook (docs/playbooks/invocation-stabilizer.md) with rollout, verification, and rollback steps - unit and integration tests + an observability CI job to validate recording rule correctness Checkout notes: this description contains the checklist, rollout plan, and links. Checklist: - [x] Stabilizer core implementation (src/observability/stabilizer.go) - [x] Recording rules and gating templates (monitoring/prometheus/rules/stabilizer.rules.yml) - [x] Dashboard (grafana/dashboards/invocation-stabilizer.json) - [x] Playbook and runbook (docs/playbooks/invocation-stabilizer.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests (pkg/observability/stabilizer_test.go, tests/integration/stabilizer_e2e.yaml) - [x] CI job (ci/observability-stabilizer.yml) - [x] Backwards-compatible metric names and opt-in feature flag (env: OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=true) Links: - Linear: ENG-1149 - Support ticket: SUP-4021 - Design doc: internal/notes/invocation-stabilizer-design.md (internal link) Rollout plan summary: 1) Deploy stabilizer behind feature flag to a small subset of serving nodes (canary) and emit stabilized metrics alongside raw metrics. 2) Observe fidelity distribution over 48h. 3) Flip Prometheus gating in read-only mode (no alert suppression) and run the CI recording-rule validation. 4) Enable gating for a small set of non-critical SLOs for 24h. 5) Gradually expand gating scope to critical SLOs and all regions. Rollback: flip OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=false or revert Prometheus gating rules. Why this is safe: stabilized metrics are emitted in parallel and metric names are opt-in; alerts are gated rather than deleted. Backwards compatibility preserved for any consumer of raw series. Performance: the stabilizer runs per-invocation in a lightweight path (1-2 allocations); measured overhead ~0.2ms per invocation in microbenchmarks (see design doc).

merge_commit_message: Introduce invocation stabilizer and fidelity-aware gating (ENG-1149) - squash
merge_summary: Merged after reviewers approved. CI green. Feature gate default off; canary rollout started.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in Invocation Stabilizer that emits stabilized latency percentiles and fidelity tags; introduces fidelity-aware alert gating to reduce noisy SRE alerts. Requires updating Prometheus recording rules during rollout. Backwards compatible and opt-in via OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER.
post_merge_actions: Create canary deployment via infra runbook: infra/recipes/deploy-stabilizer-canary.md
Notify SRE channel with verification checklist and dashboards link
Schedule 48h observation window and adjust gating thresholds if necessary
notes_for_oncall: If noise increases after gating disable Prometheus gating templates and flip OBS_INVOCATION_STABILIZER=false. Look for sudden drop in raw metric cardinality or missing stabilized series in the first 10 minutes after deployment.
